key_insight: Adding Al2O3 (3–6 wt%) to flame-sprayed Cu–Al–Ni–Fe coatings improves adhesion and microstructural quality while also increasing surface roughness.
engineering_relevance: Al2O3 reinforcement can be used to tune thermal-sprayed coating performance on stainless steel for better bonding and denser, more durable surfaces.
method: Flame-sprayed Cu–Al–Ni–Fe alloy coatings with 0, 3, and 6 wt% Al2O3 on AISI 304L stainless steel
Evaluated surface roughness and adhesion strength
Used SEM and EDS to assess microstructure and elemental composition
evidence_signal: The abstract reports roughness increasing from 5 to 8 µm and adhesion strength rising from 22 ± 0.655 MPa to 26 ± 0.818 MPa as Al2O3 content increased, along with reduced porosity and microcracks in SEM images.
watch_item: The improved properties should be balanced against the rougher surface finish, which may be a concern for applications requiring tight surface tolerances.
paper_title: Effect of Al₂O₃ Addition on the Surface Roughness, Adhesion Strength, and Microstructure of Flame-Sprayed Cu–Al–Ni–Fe Alloy Coatings
